en: The Mahāvaipulya Tathāgatagarbha Sūtra, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Buddhabhadra of India during the Eastern Jin Dynasty. Thus have I heard: At one time the Buddha was staying on Vulture Peak Mountain in the city of Rājagṛha, together with a great assembly of monks and bodhisattvas. At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the great assembly: "O sons of good family, within the bodies of all sentient beings there exists the Tathāgata-garbha, which is pure, eternal, blissful, and self-sovereign. It is like a precious jewel wrapped in a foul garment; though the garment is filthy, the jewel within remains untainted. In the same way, although sentient beings are shrouded in the defilements of afflictions, the Tathāgata-garbha within them is inherently pure and possesses the thirty-two marks of a Great Man. O sons of good family, this Tathāgata-garbha is the source from which all the Buddhas of the three times arise. It is the ultimate refuge for all sentient beings. Therefore, you should cultivate yourselves with diligence to realize this profound Dharma.

At that time, the World-Honored One, wishing to elaborate further on the meaning of this teaching, spoke these verses: "The Tathāgata-garbha is present within the bodies of all beings; It is eternally pure, endowed with the marks of a Great Man. Just as a priceless jewel may be wrapped in a foul rag, Though the rag is filthy, the jewel remains undefiled. So too, within the bodies of all sentient beings, The Tathāgata-garbha is ever-present and pure. Shrouded by the various layers of afflictions, Sentient beings do not perceive their own nature. If one can remove these afflictions through wisdom, One will behold the Buddha-nature, just as one sees the jewel. [The sūtra continues with further parables and teachings regarding the Tathāgata-garbha.]

In the Candana Multi-storied Hall of the Moon-Preaching, ten years after his attainment of Buddhahood, he was accompanied by a great assembly of one hundred thousand bhikṣus and bodhisattva-mahāsattvas as numerous as the sands of sixty Ganges Rivers—all of whom had perfected the power of great diligence, had previously made offerings to hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of Buddhas, and were all capable of turning the irreversible wheel of Dharma.

If any sentient beings hear their names, they shall never regress from the unsurpassed path. Their names are: Bodhisattva Dharmamati, Bodhisattva Siṃhamati, Bodhisattva Vajramati, Bodhisattva Vinayamati, Bodhisattva Sumati, Bodhisattva Candraprabha, Bodhisattva Ratnacandra, and Bodhisattva Pūrṇacandra.
Sādhū, the Bodhisattva Vīramati, the Bodhisattva Amitavīra, the Bodhisattva Anantavīra, the Bodhisattva Trailokyasamatikrānta,
the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, the Bodhisattva Mahāsthāmaprāpta, the Bodhisattva Gandhahastin, the Bodhisattva Gandhottama,
the Bodhisattva Gandhottamakūṭa, the Bodhisattva Śirigarbha, and the Bodhisattva Sūryagarbha.
The Bodhisattva, the Bodhisattva Dhvajaketu, the Bodhisattva Mahādhvajaketu, the Bodhisattva Vimaladhvaja,
the Bodhisattva Anantaprabha, the Bodhisattva Prabhākara, the Bodhisattva Vimalaprabha, the Bodhisattva Nandirāja, the Bodhisattva Nityananda,
the Bodhisattva Ratnapāṇi, the Bodhisattva Gaganagañja, and the Bodhisattva Vigatamada.
Mānabodhisattva, Sumerubodhisattva, Prabhāśrīrājabodhisattva, Dhāraṇīśvararājabodhisattva, Dhāraṇībodhisattva,
Sarvavyādhipraśamanabodhisattva, Sarvasattvavyādhipraśamanabodhisattva,
Nanditantrabodhisattva, Tṛptamānasabodhisattva, and Nityatṛptabodhisattva.
The Bodhisattva Universal Radiance, the Bodhisattva Moon Clarity, the Bodhisattva Jewel Wisdom,
the Bodhisattva Transformation of the Female Body, the Bodhisattva Great Thunderous Sound, the Bodhisattva Guide, the Bodhisattva Non-Vain Sight,
the Bodhisattva Sovereignty over All Dharmas, the Bodhisattva Maitreya, and the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī— thus [were they].
Sixty *gaṅgā*-sands of *bodhisattva-mahāsattvas* from immeasurable Buddha-fields,
together with countless devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas,
kiṃnaras, and mahoragas, all assembled there to pay their respects and make offerings.

At that time, the World-Honored One sat upright in samādhi within the Sandalwood Multi-storied Pavilion and manifested spiritual transformations. There appeared countless thousand-petaled lotuses, as large as chariot wheels, perfect in color and fragrance yet not yet blossomed; within every flower was a transformation Buddha. These ascended into the void, covering the world like a precious canopy. Each and every lotus emitted immeasurable light, and all the lotuses simultaneously unfolded in full splendor.

By the Buddha’s spiritual power, in an instant they all withered and transformed. Within those flowers, all the emanated Buddhas sat cross-legged, each emitting hundreds of thousands of countless rays of light. At that time, the adornments of this world-system were exceptionally sublime; the entire great assembly rejoiced and leaped for joy, marveling at this unprecedented event and all harboring doubts:
"For what cause and condition have these countless exquisite flowers suddenly withered and changed?"
"It is withered, black, foul-smelling, filthy, and utterly loathsome.
At that time, the World-Honored One, knowing the doubts of the great assembly of bodhisattvas, addressed Vajramati:
"Good son!..."
"Regarding all that you may have doubts about within the Buddha-dharma, ask whatever you wish.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Vajramati, knowing that the entire great assembly harbored doubts, addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
By what causes and conditions do these countless lotuses, each containing a transformation Buddha, ascend into the void and cover the world, only for them all to wither and change in an instant?
"Each of the emanation Buddhas emitted countless hundreds of thousands of rays of light, which the entire assembly saw and, with palms joined in reverence, paid homage to.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Vajramati spoke in verse:
"I have never before beheld Such a spiritual transformation as today's."
I beheld hundreds of thousands of billions of Buddhas, seated within those lotus-treasury worlds,
each emitting countless rays of light that completely overspread all lands.
These stainless Guides adorned every world-system.
The lotus has suddenly withered and changed; there is none who does not feel aversion and dissatisfaction.
By what causes and conditions does this divine transformation now appear?
I have beheld Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, as well as their immeasurable spiritual transformations.
"Never before have we seen anything like this; we pray that you will explain it for us in detail.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed Vajramati and the other bodhisattvas, saying: "Good sons!
“There is a Mahāvaipulya Sūtra titled ‘The Tathāgatagarbha’; because I am about to expound it, I have manifested this auspicious omen. All of you, listen attentively and reflect upon it well.
They all replied, “Excellent!”
"I wish to hear it with joy.
The Buddha said, "Good son!

Just as countless lotus flowers manifested by the Buddha suddenly withered and changed, within which were innumerable transformation Buddhas, adorned with the marks and signs of perfection, sitting cross-legged and emitting great radiance; all who beheld this marvel paid homage without exception.
"In this way, son of good family!

With my Buddha-eye I observe all sentient beings: within their afflictions of greed, anger, and ignorance, there exists the Tathāgata’s wisdom, the Tathāgata’s eye, and the Tathāgata’s body, sitting cross-legged, solemn and unmoving."
"Good son!

Although all sentient beings are within the various realms of existence, the Tathāgatagarbha exists within their bodies of affliction; it is eternally unstained and fully endowed with virtuous marks, no different from my own."
Furthermore, son of good family!

It is like a person with the divine eye who observes an unopened flower and sees within all those flowers the body of a Tathāgata sitting in the full lotus posture; once the withered petals are removed, it becomes clearly manifest.
In this way, son of good family!

Having perceived the *tathāgatagarbha* within sentient beings, the Buddha desires to cause it to blossom; therefore, he preaches the Dharma to them in order to eliminate afflictions and manifest the Buddha-nature.
"Good son!

It is the natural law of all Buddhas that whether a Buddha appears in the world or does not appear, the Tathāgatagarbha of all sentient beings is eternally present and unchanging; it is only because those sentient beings are shrouded by afflictions."
The Tathāgata appears in the world and extensively expounds the Dharma to eliminate the afflictions of dust and toil, purifying all-encompassing wisdom. Good son!

If there are bodhisattvas who believe in and delight in this Dharma, practicing and studying it with single-minded devotion, they shall attain liberation and achieve equal and perfect enlightenment, universally performing the Buddha-work for the sake of the world.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke in verse:
"Just as a withered and decaying flower, whose petals have not yet fully opened,
is seen by one with the divine eye— so too is the Tathāgata’s body, free from defilement."
Once the withered flowers have been removed, one beholds the Unobstructed Teacher;
for the sake of severing afflictions, he is the most supreme among those who transcend the world.
The Buddha observes all classes of sentient beings and sees that they all possess the Tathāgatagarbha.
Enshrouded by immeasurable afflictions, Like being entangled in foul flowers;
For the sake of all sentient beings, To eliminate their afflictions,
I universally preach the True Dharma, Causing them to swiftly attain the path of Buddhahood.
"I have seen with my Buddha-eye that within the bodies of all sentient beings, the Buddha-treasure dwells in peace; I preach the Dharma so that it may be revealed.
Furthermore, son of good family:
It is like pure honey located within a tree on a cliff, surrounded and guarded by countless swarms of bees.

At that time, there is a person possessed of skillful wisdom and expedient means who first eliminates those bees and then takes the honey, consuming it as he pleases and extending its benefit to those far and near.
In this way, son of good family!
All sentient beings possess the Tathāgatagarbha, just like that pure honey within a tree on a cliff, which is shrouded by various afflictions and guarded by swarms of bees.

With my Buddha-eye, I observe them as they truly are; employing skillful means, I preach the Dharma according to their needs, eliminating afflictions and opening the Buddha’s knowledge and vision, universally performing the work of a Buddha for the sake of the world.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke in verse:
"Just as one who seeks honey from a tree on a cliff, surrounded by immeasurable bees,
must first eliminate those swarms of bees through skillful means."
The Tathāgatagarbha of sentient beings is like honey within a tree on a cliff;
bound by the fetters and the dust of afflictions, it is guarded as if by a swarm of bees.
For the sake of all sentient beings, I employ skillful means to preach the True Dharma.
Extinguishing the bees of affliction, Revealing the Tathāgatagarbha;
Possessing unimpeded eloquence, Proclaiming the nectar-like Dharma,
Universally enabling the attainment of perfect enlightenment, With great compassion rescuing all living beings.
"Furthermore, good son!

It is like fine rice that has not yet been separated from its husks and bran; the poor and ignorant despise it, deeming it fit only for discard. Once the chaff has been removed and it is refined, it is constantly used for the imperial table."
In this way, noble son!

With my Buddha-eye I observe all sentient beings whose husks of affliction cover and obscure the Tathāgata’s immeasurable knowledge and vision. Therefore, by means of skillful methods, I preach the Dharma according to their needs, causing them to eliminate afflictions, purify all-knowledge, and become the most perfectly awakened ones within all worlds.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke in verse:
"Just as when all kinds of fine grain Have not yet had their husks and chaff removed,
The poor regard them with contempt, Considering them things fit only for discard."
Though it appears useless on the outside, its interior remains undestroyed;
once the husks and chaff have been removed, it becomes the meal of a king.
Thus I see that among the classes of sentient beings, the Buddha-treasury is concealed by afflictions.
I preach the Dharma for their eradication, so that they may attain all-knowledge.
As is my nature as a Tathāgata, so too it is with sentient beings;
I transform and instruct them to bring them to purity, so that they may swiftly accomplish the Unsurpassed Way.
"Furthermore, good son!
It is like pure gold that has fallen into an impure place, remaining hidden and unmanifest for many years; though the pure gold does not decay, no one is able to know it."
One who possesses the divine eye says to the multitude:
"Within this impurity lies a treasure of pure gold; you should extract it and enjoy it as you please.
Thus it is, O son of good family!
The impure places are the immeasurable afflictions; the true gold treasure is the Tathāgatagarbha; and those with the divine eye are the Tathāgatas.
Therefore, the Tathāgata extensively expounds the Dharma to cause all sentient beings to eliminate their afflictions, so that they may all attain perfect enlightenment and perform the Buddha-work.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke in verse:
"Like gold within impurity, It is hidden and cannot be seen;
Only one with the divine eye perceives it, And immediately informs the multitude."
"If you extract it, wash it clean, and enjoy it as you please, your kinsmen shall all share in the blessing.
Such is the Eye of the Sugata; he beholds all classes of sentient beings."
Within the mire of afflictions, the nature of the Tathāgata remains unimpaired.
Teaching the Dharma according to what is appropriate, he enables all things to be accomplished;
though Buddha-nature is shrouded by afflictions, he swiftly removes them to make it pure.
"Furthermore, good son!
It is like a poor man’s house that contains a treasury of precious jewels, yet the jewels cannot say: 'I am here. "
"Since they do not know it for themselves and there is no one to tell them, they are unable to open this precious treasure-store; all sentient beings are likewise so.

The Tathāgata’s power of knowledge and vision and his fearlessness constitute a great dharma-treasure-store within their own bodies, yet they neither hear nor know of it, becoming mired in delusion regarding the five desires, revolving through birth and death, and undergoing immeasurable suffering."

Therefore, the Buddhas appear in the world to reveal the Dharma-treasury of the Tathāgata within one's own body; they faithfully accept and purify all-knowledge, universally reveal the Tathāgata-garbha for the sake of all sentient beings, and act as great donors through their unimpeded eloquence.
"In this way, noble son!
With my Buddha-eye, I behold that all sentient beings possess the Tathāgatagarbha; therefore, I have taught this Dharma for the sake of the bodhisattvas.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke in verse:
"It is like a poor man's house, within which lies a treasury of precious jewels;
yet the master neither knows nor sees it, and the jewels themselves cannot speak.
Throughout his life he remains shrouded in ignorance, for there is no one to show him or tell him."
Possessing treasure yet unaware of it, one thus constantly encounters poverty and suffering.
With the Buddha-eye, the World-Honored One observes sentient beings:
though they wander through the five realms of rebirth, a great treasure resides within their bodies, ever-present and unchanging.
Having observed in this way, he speaks for the sake of sentient beings,
so that they may obtain the treasury of wisdom, becoming greatly wealthy and bringing vast benefit.
If they have faith in what I have said, all shall possess the treasury of jewels.
Through faith, diligence, and skillful practice, one swiftly accomplishes the unsurpassed path.
"Furthermore, son of good family!
It is like the inner kernel of an amra fruit; if it is not damaged and is planted in the earth, it will grow into a great king of trees."
Thus it is, noble son!
With my Buddha-eye I behold all sentient beings: the treasure-store of the Tathāgata lies within the shell of ignorance, just as a fruit seed resides within its rind.
"Good son!
That Tathāgatagarbha is cool and free from fever; it is a mass of great wisdom, the wondrously tranquil Nirvāṇa, and is named the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha."
“Good son!
Having thus observed sentient beings, the Tathāgata manifests this meaning for the sake of purifying the Buddha-wisdom of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke in verse:
"Just as the inner fruit of the *āmra* tree, Though its core remains unimpaired,
When planted in the great earth, Will surely become a king of great trees.
So too does the Tathāgata’s untainted eye Behold all sentient beings."
The Tathāgatagarbha within the body is like the seed within a flower or fruit.
The Buddha-treasury is shrouded by ignorance; you all should believe and know this.
It is fully endowed with the wisdom of samādhi, and nothing whatsoever can destroy it.
Therefore, I preach the Dharma to reveal that Tathāgatagarbha,
so that one may swiftly accomplish the unsurpassed path, just as a seed becomes the king of trees.
Furthermore, son of good family!

It is, for example, like a person who carries a statue of pure gold and travels to another country; passing through perilous roads and fearing robbery, he wraps it in tattered rags so that no one will recognize it.
This man suddenly passed away on the road, whereupon the golden image was abandoned in the wilderness; passersby trod upon it, regarding it as impure.
One who possessed the divine eye saw that within this tattered object lay a true golden image, and immediately brought it forth, paying it all due reverence.
"Thus it is, good son!

I see that sentient beings, with their various afflictions, transmigrate through birth and death for a long night and immeasurable time; yet the wondrous treasury of the Tathāgata exists within their bodies, solemn and pure, no different from my own."
"For this reason, the Buddha preaches the Dharma for sentient beings to sever their afflictions and purify the wisdom of the Tathāgata, further transforming and guiding all the worlds.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke in verse:
"Just as a person carrying a golden image Sets out on a journey to another land,"
Wrapped in filthy and impure things, it was cast away in the wilderness.
One with the divine eye saw it and immediately informed the multitude;
having removed the filth to reveal the true image, all were filled with great joy.
My divine eye is likewise; I behold those classes of sentient beings, entangled by evil karma and afflictions, fully possessed of the manifold sufferings of birth and death.
Furthermore, I see those sentient beings amidst the dust and grime of ignorance.
The nature of the Tathāgata is immovable, and none can destroy it.
Having seen this, the Buddha taught it to the bodhisattvas:
that the various afflictions and evil karmas shroud and obscure the most supreme body.
"One should diligently purify and sever [all obscurations] to manifest the wisdom of the Tathāgata,
which all devas, humans, nāgas, and spirits alike revere and look up to.
Furthermore, son of good family:

For example, it is like a woman who is poor, lowly, and ugly, loathed by all people, yet she carries a noble son destined to become a holy wheel-turning monarch (cakravartin) ruling over the four continents;
unaware that time has passed, she constantly regards herself as inferior and imagines her child to be one born of low status.
In this way, good son!

The Tathāgata observes all sentient beings revolving through birth and death and undergoing various bitter sufferings; yet within their bodies there is the treasure-store of the Tathāgata, just like that woman who was unaware of it.
Therefore, the Tathāgata universally preaches the Dharma for them, saying:
"Good sons! Do not disparage yourselves.

Each of you possesses Buddha-nature within your own bodies; if you exert diligent effort to extinguish all faults and evils, you shall receive the titles of Bodhisattva and World-Honored One, transforming and delivering immeasurable sentient beings."
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke in verse:
"Just as a poor woman, Whose appearance was most common and ugly,
Yet bore a son of noble marks Who was destined to become a wheel-turning monarch."
Though endowed with the seven treasures and all virtues, and ruling over the four continents,
he was unable to realize this, constantly harboring thoughts of inferiority.
As I observe all sentient beings, they too are thus entangled in suffering.
Bearing the Tathāgatagarbha within, yet unaware of it oneself;
for this reason, I tell the Bodhisattvas: "Be careful not to disparage yourselves.
Within your own bodies is the Tathāgatagarbha, which constantly possesses the light that saves the world."
If one diligently cultivates vigor, before long one will sit at the site of enlightenment and achieve the path of supreme perfect awakening, delivering and liberating immeasurable multitudes.
Furthermore, son of good family!

It is like a master caster who fashions an image of pure gold; once it has been cast, he turns it upside down on the ground. Although the exterior appears scorched and black, the interior image remains unchanged. When the mold is opened and the image is extracted, its golden hue shines with brilliant radiance.
Thus it is, noble son!
The Tathāgata observes that all sentient beings possess the Buddha-treasure within their bodies, complete with all the marks of excellence.

Having observed this, he extensively explains it for them; those sentient beings thereby attain rest and coolness, and with vajra-like wisdom they strike and shatter their afflictions, revealing the pure Buddha-body like a golden image emerging from its mold.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke in verse:
"Just as when a great smith casts An image of immeasurable pure gold,
The fool, looking at it from the outside, Sees only scorched black earth."
When the master caster perceives it has cooled, he opens the mold and the substance appears;
once all impurities have been removed, the marks and signs are vividly revealed.
With my Buddha-eye I observe that the nature of sentient beings is just like this.
Within the mire of afflictions, The nature of the Tathāgata exists in all.
Bestowing the wisdom of the vajra, One hews away the mold of afflictions;
The Tathāgatagarbha is revealed, Like pure gold made manifest.
"As I have observed, I shall instruct all bodhisattvas:
'You must receive and uphold this well, and transform all sentient beings.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Vajramati:

“Whether they be renunciants or householders, if sons or daughters of good family receive, uphold, read, recite, copy, and make offerings to this *Tathāgatagarbha Sūtra*, and explain it extensively for others, the merit they obtain will be immeasurable.”

Vajramati! Suppose there were a bodhisattva who, for the sake of the Buddha-way, diligently practiced with vigor and cultivated supernormal powers (*abhijñā*), entering various samādhis desiring to plant the roots of merit. He would make offerings to all the Buddhas currently existing, more numerous than the sands of the Ganges; he would construct seven-jeweled pavilions more numerous than the sands of the Ganges, each ten *yojanas* in height and one *yojana* square in length and breadth, providing beds of the seven jewels spread with celestial silks. For each and every Buddha, day after day, he would construct and establish pavilions of the seven jewels more numerous than the sands of the Ganges, using them to offer to each Tathāgata, as well as to the assemblies of bodhisattvas and śrāvakas.

With such things, he universally made offerings to all the Buddhas of the present, more numerous than the sands of the Ganges; continuing in this sequence until he had offered fifty times as many jeweled pavilions as there are sands in fifty Ganges Rivers, thereby honoring more than fifty times as many Buddhas of the present, along with their assemblies of Bodhisattvas and Śrāvakas, for as long as immeasurable hundreds of thousands of myriads of kalpas.
Vajramati! It is not as good as someone who, delighting in bodhi, upholds, recites, copies, and makes offerings to even a single parable from the Tathāgatagarbha Sūtra.

Vajramati! Although the roots of goodness and merit planted by these sons of good family under the various Buddhas are immeasurable, they do not equal even a hundredth part, nor a thousandth part, of the merit obtained by these sons and daughters of good family; indeed, they cannot be reached even by calculation or analogy.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke again in verse:
"If a person seeks bodhi and hears and upholds this sutra,
copies it and makes offerings to it, even if only for a single verse,"
If one should momentarily give rise to sympathetic joy for the subtle and wondrous treasury of the Tathāgata,
and listen to this true teaching, their merit shall be immeasurable.
If a person seeks bodhi and abides in great supernormal powers,
Desiring to make offerings to the Buddhas of the ten directions and their assemblies of Bodhisattvas and Śrāvakas,
numbering more than the sands of the Ganges, for inconceivable billions of years,
[one] constructs exquisite jeweled terraces for each and every Buddha.
The platform is ten yojanas high, forty li in length and breadth;
in its center is established a throne of the seven treasures, adorned with every kind of exquisite ornament.
It is spread with celestial silk cushions, each according to its seat being distinct and unique.
If one were to offer [gifts] as numerous as the sands of immeasurable Ganges Rivers to the Buddha and the great assembly,
dedicating them all in this manner, day and night without ceasing for a full hundred thousand million kalpas— the merit obtained would be just like this.
If a wise person hears this sutra and is able to uphold even a single parable and explain it to others,
their merit shall exceed that [of the former],
such that it cannot be reached by calculation or even by analogy.
The refuge of all sentient beings, Quickly accomplishing the unsurpassed path;
The Bodhisattva, through profound contemplation, Of the extremely deep Tathāgatagarbha,
Knowing that all sentient beings possess it, Swiftly accomplishes the unsurpassed path.
At that time, the World-Honored One again addressed the Bodhisattva Vajramati, saying:
"In the past, immeasurable, boundless, inconceivable, and incalculable *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas ago—indeed, even beyond such numbers."

At that time there was a Buddha, named Constantly Emitting Radiance King Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidyācaraṇasaṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, Buddha, Bhagavān.
Vajramati! For what reason is he named King Who Constantly Emits Radiance?

When that Buddha was originally practicing the bodhisattva path, as his spirit descended into his mother’s womb, he constantly emitted radiance that thoroughly illuminated lands as numerous as the atoms within a thousand buddha-worlds throughout the ten directions.

If there are sentient beings who behold this light, they will all rejoice; their afflictions will be entirely extinguished, and they will be endowed with physical strength and vitality, achieving mindfulness and wisdom, and attaining unimpeded eloquence.
If those in the hells, hungry ghosts, animals, the realm of Yama, or among the asuras behold this light, they shall all leave the evil realms and be reborn among devas and humans.
If any devas or humans behold this radiance, they shall attain non-retrogression from the unsurpassed path and be endowed with the five supernormal powers.
Those who have attained non-retrogression shall all obtain the fifty merits of the *anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti* and the *parivarta-dhāraṇī*.

Vajramati! Those lands illuminated by that light are all pure and adorned like celestial lapis lazuli. Golden cords demarcate the eightfold paths, and various jewel trees are lush with flowers and fruits, their fragrances wafting forth. When stirred by a gentle breeze, they produce sublime sounds, proclaiming the virtues of the Triple Gem and of Bodhisattvas—their faculties, powers, factors of awakening, path, meditative concentrations, and liberations.
All sentient beings who hear this shall attain the joy of the Dharma; their faith and delight will become firm, and they will forever leave behind the evil realms. O Vajramati!
Because all sentient beings in the lands of the ten directions have been touched by this light, they join their palms in reverent worship throughout the six periods of day and night.

Vajramati! That bodhisattva, from the time he dwells in the womb and is born, until his attainment of Buddhahood and his parinirvāṇa without remainder, constantly emits radiance; even after his parinirvāṇa, his stūpas and shrines continue to emit light.
For these reasons, the devas and people of the world called him King Constantly Emitting Radiance. "Vajramati!

When the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha King Constantly Emitting Radiance first attained Buddhahood, there was in his Dharma a bodhisattva named Boundless Light, who had two billion bodhisattvas as his retinue."

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Amitābha, in the presence of that Buddha, inquired about the *Tathāgatagarbha Sūtra*. The Buddha expounded it for him, remaining seated upon a single seat for fifty great kalpas; out of his protective mindfulness for all bodhisattvas, he proclaimed its sound throughout hundreds of thousands of buddha-fields as numerous as the atoms within ten buddha-worlds, teaching the Mahāyāna scripture of the *Tathāgatagarbha* through countless causes and conditions and hundreds of thousands of parables for the sake of the bodhisattvas.

When the various bodhisattvas heard this sutra being preached, they received, upheld, read, recited, and practiced it according to the teaching; with the exception of four bodhisattvas, they have all already attained Buddhahood. Vajramati!
Do not view this otherwise. Could that Bodhisattva Boundless Light be anyone else?
It is none other than myself.
Those four bodhisattvas who have not yet attained buddhahood are Mañjuśrī, Avalokiteśvara, Mahāsthāmaprāpta, and you, Vajramati. Vajramati!
“The Tathāgatagarbha Sūtra is able to bring great benefit; whoever hears it shall all attain the Buddha-way.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke again in verse:
“In incalculable kalpas past, there was a Buddha named King of Radiance.”
Constantly emitting great radiance, it universally illumines immeasurable lands.
When the Bodhisattva Boundless Light first questioned this sutra upon the Buddha’s initial attainment of the Way,
the Buddha immediately expounded it for him.
Those who have encountered the Most Victorious One and heard this sutra have all already attained Buddhahood, with the exception of four bodhisattvas:
Mañjuśrī, Avalokiteśvara, Mahāsthāmaprāpta, and Vajramati.
These four bodhisattvas and others, All have previously heard this Dharma.
Vajramati is their foremost son of supernatural powers;
At that time he was named Anantaprabha, And has already heard this sutra.
When I originally sought the Way, at the place of the Buddha Siṃhadhvaja, I also received this sutra;
as I heard it taught, I practiced accordingly.
By virtue of these roots of goodness, I have swiftly attained the path of Buddhahood.
Therefore, all bodhisattvas should uphold and expound this sutra;
having heard it, they should practice as taught, and they shall attain Buddhahood just as I do now.
Those who uphold this sutra should be honored like the World-Honored One himself.
Whoever obtains this sutra is called a lord of the Buddha-dharma;
they shall be a protector of the world, praised by all Buddhas.
If there are those who uphold this sutra, such persons are named Dharma Kings.
"He is the eye of the world; he should be praised as the World-Honored One.

When the World-Honored One had finished speaking this sutra, Vajramati and all the bodhisattvas, the fourfold assembly, and the devas, humans, gandharvas, asuras, and others, having heard what the Buddha taught, rejoiced and practiced accordingly.
